findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, exposing the database to direct connections from the internet rather than restricting it to the private application layer.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the database data at rest is not encrypted, violating the requirement to encrypt data at rest by default.

The master password is sourced from var.password and injected directly into the instance; combined with its use in user_data, this leads to credential exposure and static long-lived database credentials with no rotation or secrets manager use.

findings.issue_category: secrets exposed in instance metadata/user data
findings.description: The user_data script embeds the database password and username in plaintext, which is readable by anyone with EC2 describe-instance-attribute permissions or console access to the instance metadata, a much wider audience than the secrets store.
The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", far exceeding least privilege for an application server and effectively granting broad administrative capability over these services.
The security group rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path from the database tier.

No parameter enforcing SSL/TLS connections (e.g., require_secure_transport) is set in the associated parameter group, and the option/parameter groups do not enforce encrypted connections to MySQL, allowing unencrypted client-database traffic.

The instance profile attaches catalog_app_role, which via its inline policy grants excessive wildcard permissions to any process running on the EC2 instance, expanding the blast radius of instance compromise.
